title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
authors: Di Lisio, F.; Soilleux, E. J.; Jaeckle, F.
abstract: BackgroundMachine Learning (ML) has shown promise in histopathological diagnosis, but rare tumours, like duodenal epithelial neoplasms, are challenging because large, labelled datasets are difficult to assemble. We propose a data-efficient ML pipeline for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia in whole-slide images. MethodsWe assembled a five-hospital dataset of haematoxylin and eosin-stained duodenal biopsy whole slide images (WSIs) at 10x magnification, comprising 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic biopsies, including adenomas, carcinomas and neuroendocrine tumours. WSIs were divided into patches and encoded using the Hibou-B foundation model. We compared global standardisation with unsupervised site-specific standardisation of patch embeddings. Our pipeline combined principal component analysis, a Gaussian mixture model and a Random Forest classifier. We assessed generalisability using leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation across four hospitals and on an independent test set from a fifth hospital. ResultsIn leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation, the pipeline achieved a mean accuracy of 90%, sensitivity of 96%, specificity of 83% and an AUC of 0.96. On the external test hospital, it achieved 94% accuracy, 93% sensitivity, 95% specificity, and AUC of 0.97. Site-specific standardisation improved mean cross-validation accuracy by 20 percentage points compared with global standardisation, while the Gaussian mixture pipeline improved accuracy by 12 percentage points compared with mean pooling of patch embeddings. ConclusionsWe present a data-efficient ML approach for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia from WSIs. Strong performance was maintained across hospitals and on an independent external test cohort despite the limited number of neoplastic training cases, supporting the feasibility of foundation-model-based approaches for rare histopathological diagnoses.

infographic.key_insight: A foundation-model-based, data-efficient pipeline can detect duodenal epithelial neoplasia in whole-slide biopsy images with strong cross-hospital generalizability despite few rare-tumour cases.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This could help pathology workflows flag rare duodenal neoplasms earlier and more consistently, especially where annotated training data are limited.
method: 5-hospital H&E duodenal biopsy WSI dataset (8,027 normal; 401 neoplastic) at 10x
Patch embeddings from the Hibou-B foundation model with site-specific standardisation
PCA + Gaussian mixture model + Random Forest classifier, evaluated with leave-one-hospital-out and external testing
infographic.evidence_signal: Performance was 90% mean accuracy (AUC 0.96) in leave-one-hospital-out validation and 94% accuracy (AUC 0.97) on an independent external hospital test set.
infographic.watch_item: Results come from a retrospective, multi-centre dataset and need prospective validation before routine deployment across broader lab settings.
infographic.paper_title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study

title: A spatial AI-based biomarker with independent prognostic value in early low- and intermediate- risk breast cancer
authors: Boissin, C.; Xiang, Y.; Liu, B.; Vallon-Christersson, J.; Walker, E.; Hartman, J.; Rantalainen, M.
abstract: BackgroundPatients with ER-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer of low or intermediate grade are generally considered to have a favourable prognosis, yet a number will recur. This risk is poorly captured by standard clinicopathological factors. AI-based medical devices for whole slide image (WSI) analyses used for risk-stratification often predict on slide-level thereby overlooking spatial localisation of the biomarkers. We hypothesise that the spatial distribution of a previously reported AI-based marker provides independent prognostic value beyond its global score. Patients and MethodsThis Swedish multicentre cohort study includes 6106 patients with primary invasive breast cancer: 3078 from the Stockholm region (training) and 3028 from Sk[a]ne (independent test). Tile-level high-grade morphology scores were generated with ViT_DG, a vision-transformer adaptation of DeepGrade, and the presence of clusters of high-risk tiles localised at the invasive tumour front was defined as a binary biomarker. Primary analyses were pre-specified in the ER-positive/HER2-negative/lymph-node-negative and Grade 1-2 subgroup. Association with breast-cancer recurrence-free interval (BCRFI) and distant metastasis were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models (HR). ResultsIn the primary subgroup (n=1536 training; n=1403 test), tumour front clusters were present in 37% and 39% of patients. Cluster-positive status was associated with a 2.30-fold increased risk in the external test. Cluster-negative patients achieved a 10-year BCRFI of 95.3%, equivalent to Grade 1 patients and better than Grade 2 (92.4%), whereas cluster-positive patients (90.2%) did worse than the Grade 3 reference. The association was retained in patients classified as low-risk by ViT_DG (test set multivariable HR 2.86), identifying high-risk patients not captured by the global score. ConclusionsThe absence of high-risk morphology clusters at the tumour front is an independent prognostic indicator, identifying a low-risk group independently of the global AI biomarker classification. More broadly, preserving the spatial distribution of AI-derived predictions enables prognostic stratification beyond slide-level aggregation. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02306096

infographic.key_insight: A spatial AI biomarker that detects high-risk morphology clusters at the invasive tumor front adds independent prognostic value beyond the overall slide score in early low- and intermediate-risk breast cancer.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This approach may better identify which patients with ER-positive/HER2-negative disease are truly low risk versus those who still need closer follow-up or additional treatment consideration.
method: 6106 Swedish breast cancer cases were split into a Stockholm training cohort and an independent Skåne test cohort.
A vision-transformer model (ViT_DG) scored tile-level high-grade morphology on whole-slide images.
A binary biomarker was defined by the presence of high-risk tile clusters at the invasive tumor front and tested with multivariable Cox models.
infographic.evidence_signal: In the ER-positive/HER2-negative/lymph-node-negative, grade 1-2 subgroup, cluster-positive status predicted worse recurrence outcomes, with an external test-set hazard ratio of 2.30 and retained value even among cases labeled low-risk by the global AI score.
infographic.watch_item: This is retrospective, pathology-image based evidence from a Swedish cohort, so external validation and workflow standardization are still needed before routine implementation.
infographic.paper_title: A spatial AI-based biomarker with independent prognostic value in early low- and intermediate- risk breast cancer

title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
authors: Rohani, F.; Mostafavi, S.; Ebrahimifakhar, P.; Zomorrodi, R.; Mueller, A.
abstract: BackgroundAttention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity that significantly affect cognitive, academic, and social functioning. Although electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising non-invasive tool for identifying objective neurophysiological biomarkers of ADHD because of its high temporal resolution and cost-effectiveness, many existing machine learning studies rely on single-domain EEG features, which may not adequately capture the complex functional organization of the brain. MethodsThis study proposes a subject-level EEG classification framework that integrates three complementary feature domains: spectral characteristics, weighted Phase Lag Index (wPLI)-based functional connectivity, and topological descriptors derived from persistent homology. EEG recordings from 121 subjects were preprocessed and segmented into overlapping windows for feature extraction. Window-level features were aggregated to generate subject-level representations. Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) was employed to select the 110 most informative features from an initial set of 1,043 descriptors. Five machine learning classifiers, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), were evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation. An ablation study was further conducted to assess the contribution of each feature domain. Model interpretability was investigated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), two widely adopted Explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques for interpreting machine learning models. ResultsAmong the evaluated classifiers, the SVM achieved the highest classification performance, yielding an accuracy of 80.17%, an F1-score of 80.95%, a balanced accuracy of 80.14%, a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 86.72%, and a precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 87.34%. The ablation study demonstrated that combining spectral, functional connectivity, and topological features consistently outperformed individual feature domains, highlighting the complementary nature of these representations. Explainable AI analyses further identified functional connectivity features as the primary contributors to classification performance while confirming the additional value of spectral and topological descriptors. ConclusionsThe proposed framework demonstrates that integrating spectral analysis, functional connectivity, and topological data analysis provides an effective and interpretable approach for subject-level ADHD classification from EEG recordings. The combination of recursive feature selection, multi-domain feature fusion, ablation analysis, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence establishes a transparent and reproducible pipeline that may facilitate the development of reliable EEG-based clinical decision-support systems for ADHD.

infographic.key_insight: A multi-domain EEG model combining spectral, connectivity, and topological features improved subject-level ADHD classification, with SVM performing best.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This work suggests a more informative, interpretable EEG-based approach for supporting ADHD research and future biomarker development, though it is not a clinical diagnostic tool.
method: 121-subject EEG dataset preprocessed into overlapping windows
Extracted 1,043 features across spectral, wPLI connectivity, and persistent homology domains
Applied recursive feature elimination and compared five classifiers with five-fold cross-validation
infographic.evidence_signal: Using stratified five-fold cross-validation, the top SVM model reached 80.17% accuracy, 80.95% F1-score, 86.72% ROC-AUC, and 87.34% PR-AUC.
infographic.watch_item: Performance was evaluated on a relatively small sample, so external validation on independent datasets is needed before broader use.
infographic.paper_title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification

title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study
authors: Cao, Z.; Xie, D.; Zou, S.; Li, D.; Martinez-Martinez, P.; Zong, S.; Zhang, Z.
abstract: Tissue-based assays provide broad screening for neural autoantibodies but remain vulnerable to technical and reader-dependent variability. We evaluated an integrated workflow combining automated 3,3'-diaminobenzidine tissue-based assay processing, digital whole-slide imaging, and interpretable deep learning. Model development used 2,357 retrospective serum and cerebrospinal fluid images referred from more than 80 institutions and processed in a centralized laboratory, with reference labels established by expert-consensus tissue-based assay interpretation. A prospective validation cohort included 200 images from 200 unique patients (154 positive and 46 negative; 100 serum and 100 cerebrospinal fluid). The same images were evaluated by two expert and two novice readers in a fixed-order two-round study, with unaided interpretation followed by artificial-intelligence-assisted interpretation after a washout of at least two weeks. The standalone binary classifier achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.922, accuracy of 86.5%, sensitivity of 85.7%, and specificity of 89.1% in prospective validation. Pooled reader accuracy was 90.4% in the unaided round and 97.4% in the artificial-intelligence-assisted round (McNemar P < 0.001), with specificity of 82.6% and 99.5%, respectively. Novice-reader accuracy was 83.3% unaided and 96.5% with artificial-intelligence assistance (P < 0.001), approaching unaided expert accuracy of 97.5%. Among tissue-based-assay-positive cases, reader accuracy for cytoplasmic/nuclear antigen-associated versus neural surface antigen-associated staining-pattern subclassification was 88.8% unaided and 94.0% with artificial-intelligence assistance (P < 0.001). These findings support further multicentre, cross-platform evaluation of artificial-intelligence-assisted neural autoantibody tissue interpretation. Abbreviated summaryCao et al. report prospective validation of an automated tissue-based neural autoantibody workflow combining digital imaging and interpretable deep learning. Artificial-intelligence-assisted reading was associated with higher interpretation accuracy, particularly among less-experienced readers, supporting further multicentre validation across laboratories and imaging platforms.

infographic.key_insight: An AI-assisted workflow for tissue-based antibody interpretation improved accuracy, especially for novice readers, compared with unaided interpretation.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This could help standardize autoimmune encephalitis autoantibody screening and reduce reader-dependent variability in centralized laboratory workflows.
method: Trained an interpretable deep-learning model on 2,357 retrospective serum and CSF tissue-based assay images from >80 institutions.
Prospectively validated the system on 200 new images from 200 unique patients using expert-consensus labels.
Compared two experts and two novices reading the same cases unaided versus with AI assistance after a washout period.
infographic.evidence_signal: In prospective validation, the standalone classifier achieved AUROC 0.922 and the AI-assisted reader round raised pooled accuracy from 90.4% to 97.4% (McNemar P < 0.001).
infographic.watch_item: Results come from a centralized, prospective validation setting, so multicenter cross-platform performance and real-world workflow robustness still need confirmation.
infographic.paper_title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study

title: A Blood-Based Synaptic Biomarker in Neuronally-Enriched Extracellular Vesicles Predicts Disability Progression in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis
authors: Jank, L.; Kumar, M. K. S.; Joshi, D.; Minney, V.; Eskinder, R.; Thapa, R.; Heller, J. G.; Filippatou, A. G.; Siavoshi, F.; Smith, M. D.; Harp, C.; Abioye, I.; Sotirchos, E. S.; Dewey, B. E.; Saidha, S.; Fitzgerald, K. C.; Calabresi, P. A.; Mowry, E. M.; Bhargava, P.
abstract: Progressive multiple sclerosis (PMS) lacks blood-based biomarkers of the neurodegenerative processes driving disability. We measured synaptopodin, a postsynaptic protein, in neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicles (NEVs) across two independent cohorts: the SPRINT-MS trial (n=184) and a real-world validation cohort (n=268). A one SD increase in baseline synaptopodin was associated with [~]32% lower risk of confirmed disability progression in PMS (p=0.011), with the strongest effect in secondary PMS (SPMS) ([~]57% lower odds, p=0.019). This SPMS association was replicated in the validation cohort ([~]60% lower odds, p=0.009). Higher baseline synaptopodin was associated with future slower whole-brain atrophy and preserved microstructural integrity across MRI metrics (p=0.007-0.013). Longitudinal changes in NEV synaptopodin were associated with disability worsening (p=0.007) and paralleled MRI microstructural changes. NEV synaptopodin, but not NfL, was associated with confirmed disability progression in PMS participants with both biomarkers measured (HR 0.71 vs 1.12, p=0.007 vs 0.22 for NEV synaptopodin and NfL, respectively) and SPMS (HR 0.58 vs 1.10, p=0.003 vs 0.50). Adding synaptopodin, but not NfL, to a base model improved discrimination for disability progression in SPMS in both cohorts (e.g. validation AUC 0.755 to 0.838, p=0.005). These findings identify NEV synaptopodin as a prognostic and longitudinal, blood biomarker of synaptic integrity in PMS, particularly SPMS, complementing NfL.

infographic.key_insight: Neuronally-enriched extracellular vesicle synaptopodin in blood is a prognostic marker of disability progression and brain integrity decline in progressive multiple sclerosis, especially SPMS.
infographic.clinical_relevance: If validated broadly, this blood-based biomarker could help identify progressive MS patients at higher risk of worsening and improve monitoring beyond neurofilament light chain alone.
method: Measured synaptopodin in neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicles from blood
Tested associations in two cohorts: SPRINT-MS (n=184) and a real-world validation cohort (n=268)
Linked baseline and longitudinal biomarker levels to disability progression and MRI outcomes
infographic.evidence_signal: Across two cohorts, higher baseline NEV synaptopodin was associated with lower risk of confirmed disability progression and stronger MRI preservation signals, with replication in the validation cohort and added predictive value over NfL in SPMS.
infographic.watch_item: This is an observational biomarker study, so clinical utility will depend on external validation, assay standardization, and clear thresholds for use in practice.
infographic.paper_title: A Blood-Based Synaptic Biomarker in Neuronally-Enriched Extracellular Vesicles Predicts Disability Progression in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis

title: Efficiency of a Multi-step Screening and Enrichment Process for Prospective Sepsis Cohort Enrollment
authors: Cosimi, L. A.; Qi, W.; Naz-McLean, S.; Pan, K.; Li, S.; Laibinis, H. H.; Rooney, A. R.; Moran, C.; Valentine, G. C.; Hwang, S.; Deguine, J.; Pickard, J.; Hung, D. T.; Woolley, A. E.
abstract: BackgroundHost response and biomarker research to advance sepsis therapeutics requires well-characterized cohorts with longitudinal biospecimens across a range of hosts and infections. Automated screening based on SIRS criteria is sensitive but nonspecific and identifies more candidates than research teams can approach, sample, and follow longitudinally. We evaluated a structured enrichment review by non-physician study staff, done after automated screening in a hospital-wide prospective sepsis cohort. MethodsThe CISID cohort is a prospective observational study of hospitalized patients with suspected sepsis, enrolling adults from the ED, inpatient wards, and ICUs at a tertiary academic medical center. Patients were identified through: (1) automated electronic health record screening for two or more SIRS criteria with a 24-hour lookback, documentation of microbiologic culture or PCR, and receipt of a new antibiotic; (2) a sepsis enrichment step of structured chart review by trained non-physician study staff; and (3) discussion with the primary clinical team. Enrolled patients underwent physician adjudication into four diagnostic categories. To evaluate the enrichment step, we analyzed all patients screened during a 9-week period, assigned a composite "sepsis-likely" variable (CDC Adult Sepsis Event criteria or ICD-10 code R65.20/R65.21 within 48 hours before or after screening), and assessed mortality across each stage of screening. We also assessed concordance of the composite with physician adjudication among enrolled patients. ResultsFrom November 2023 through February 2026, 4,318 patients screened in through EHR-based automated screening; 1,220 (28%) were flagged for enrollment, and 288 were enrolled. Physician adjudication classified 209 (73%) as sepsis, 46 (16%) as infection without sepsis, 14 (5%) were classified as undifferentiated critical illness, and 19 (6.6%) as non-infectious sepsis mimics. Patients with sepsis were severely ill (median SOFA score, 9; ICU admission, 80%; shock, 48%), and 51% were immunocompromised; mortality was 14% in hospital and 27% at 90 days. In a 9-week sample of 907 screened encounters, 21% of those deferred and 70% of those flagged for enrollment met the sepsis-likely composite, a 3.3-fold increase in prevalence after structured study team review. ConclusionsA brief structured enrichment review after automated screening tripled the prevalence of EHR-based sepsis indicators among patients selected for enrollment, while concentrating enrollment efforts on roughly one-quarter of screened-in patients in this hospital-wide, all-source suspected-sepsis cohort. This approach may help prospective cohorts direct limited biospecimen resources toward patients most informative for host-response and biomarker research.

infographic.key_insight: A two-step screening workflow—automated EHR flagging followed by structured non-physician chart review—substantially narrows a large candidate pool to a higher-yield prospective sepsis cohort.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This approach may improve efficiency for enrolling well-characterized sepsis patients for biomarker and host-response studies, while reducing burden on clinical teams and study staff.
method: Automated EHR screening for SIRS criteria, microbiologic testing, and new antibiotic use
Structured enrichment review by trained non-physician staff
Primary team discussion plus physician adjudication into diagnostic categories
infographic.evidence_signal: In 4,318 screened patients, 1,220 (28%) were flagged and 288 enrolled; among enrolled patients, 73% were adjudicated as sepsis, supporting enrichment of the final cohort.
infographic.watch_item: The workflow may improve cohort quality but still depends on local EHR data capture, staff expertise, and site-specific adjudication practices, which could limit generalizability.
infographic.paper_title: Efficiency of a Multi-step Screening and Enrichment Process for Prospective Sepsis Cohort Enrollment

title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies Prominent Epicardial Adipose Tissue Associated With an Adverse Cardiometabolic Profile
authors: Aminorroaya, A.; Coppi, A.; McNamara, R. L.; Lima, J. A. C.; Krumholz, H. M.; Antoniades, C.; Khera, R.; Oikonomou, E. K.
abstract: BackgroundExcess epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) dysfunction, but its assessment has traditionally required advanced imaging. ObjectivesWe investigated whether AI-enabled echocardiography could characterize epicardial adiposity and identify residual cardiometabolic risk beyond body mass index (BMI). MethodsWe developed PanAdipo, a video-based deep learning model in 1,114,441 videos from 28,797 studies across the Yale-New Haven Health System (YNHHS; 2016-2022), using report-derived expert reader labels of prominent EAT (2.3% of studies). PanAdipo was evaluated in five cohorts: a temporally distinct YNHHS transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) set (n=4,588 patients contributing 5,130 studies), an emergency department point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) cohort (n=10,957), the geographically distinct MIMIC-IV dataset (n=4,549), the community-based Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA Exam 6, n=2,740), and in held-out YNHHS patients with paired coronary CT angiography within 12 months (n=5,167). Analyses examined discrimination of the report label and of CT-defined high indexed EAT volume, correlation with paired cardiac CT phenotypes, and BMI-adjusted associations with cardiometabolic biomarkers and newly documented metabolic disease. ResultsIn the held-out health system test set, PanAdipo identified prominent EAT documented in clinical reports with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.86 (95% CI, 0.82-0.91) across all views and of up to 0.93 when combining apical 4-chamber and parasternal views. Against paired CT-derived measurements, PanAdipo discriminated age- and sex-specific high EAT (EAT/heart volume [≥]95th percentile) with AUROCs of 0.91 to 0.95 across age-sex groups and correlated more strongly with indexed EAT volume ({rho}=0.76) than with BMI ({rho}=0.41, all P<0.001); PanAdipo alone explained 53% of indexed EAT volume variance, versus 23% for age, sex, and BMI combined. In MESA, higher scores were associated with an adverse metabolic profile (higher HOMA-IR [{beta}=0.17 per SD; 95% CI, 0.11-0.22]) after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. In health system TTE and POCUS cohorts, higher scores were associated with newly documented MASLD/MASH (BMI-adjusted HRpooled 1.31 [1.03-1.67] per SD of log[PanAdipo]) and hyperlipidemia (1.11 [1.04-1.18]). ConclusionsAI-enabled echocardiography provides a scalable digital biomarker that characterizes prominent epicardial adiposity and is associated with an adverse cardiometabolic profile, highlighting a role for echocardiography in metabolic risk stratification. CONDENSED ABSTRACTEpicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is linked to cardiometabolic risk, but its assessment has traditionally required advanced imaging. We developed PanAdipo, a deep learning model that derives a digital biomarker of EAT from routine echocardiography. PanAdipo tracks CT-defined epicardial adiposity ({rho}=0.76; AUROC 0.91-0.95 for age-/sex-specific high indexed-EAT), yet correlates modestly with body mass index (BMI; {rho}=0.19-0.41). After BMI adjustment, higher scores were associated with insulin resistance in a community-based cohort and newly documented metabolic disease across health systems. AI-enabled echocardiography may provide a scalable window into epicardial adiposity, with potential applications for enriching trial populations and monitoring response to cardiometabolic therapies.

infographic.key_insight: AI-enabled echocardiography can detect prominent epicardial adipose tissue and uncover cardiometabolic risk that is not explained by BMI alone.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This approach could help clinicians flag patients with hidden epicardial fat burden using routine ultrasound, supporting earlier risk stratification without requiring advanced imaging.
method: Trained the PanAdipo deep learning model on 1,114,441 echocardiography videos from 28,797 studies labeled by expert report review.
Validated the model across multiple external cohorts, including TTE, POCUS, MIMIC-IV, MESA, and paired cardiac CT datasets.
Compared AI scores with CT-defined epicardial adipose tissue and with cardiometabolic biomarkers and newly documented metabolic disease.
infographic.evidence_signal: PanAdipo achieved AUROC 0.86 for report-labeled prominent EAT and up to 0.95 for CT-defined high EAT, while correlating more strongly with indexed EAT volume (rho=0.76) than BMI (rho=0.41).
infographic.watch_item: Performance was strongest in retrospective, multi-cohort validation, so prospective testing and workflow integration are still needed before routine deployment.
infographic.paper_title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies Prominent Epicardial Adipose Tissue Associated With an Adverse Cardiometabolic Profile
